trigger.summary: The unfinished ten-tool layer installs capabilities but does not make the agent select and use them as one workflow.
trigger.root_cause: Catalog membership, process orchestration, and always-active MCP routing were conflated; a disabled summarizer and the process router were counted as code-intelligence tools while no route emitted a task-specific tool sequence.
trigger.evidence_ref: _reference/code-intelligence-tools.json tools[2,7]; .mcp.json codesight.disabled; scripts/lib/code-intelligence-policy.js exports without task workflow; scripts/codex-route-task.js route result

posture_evidence.summary: The released template is consumed by heterogeneous downstream repositories and is still being actively evolved.

protected_contracts.sot: Existing .mcp.json entries and template sync preservation rules

product.user_victory: A downstream agent retrieves structural code context with fewer irrelevant file reads while the operator can see exactly what is installed, active, healthy, and measured.
product.final_path: Template rollout detects the stack, installs pinned tools, activates only useful capabilities, verifies health, and records comparable context-efficiency evidence.
product.falsifier: The rollout adds tool noise or installation cost without reducing representative exploration tokens and tool calls at equivalent answer quality.

change.summary: Replace the decorative catalog with ten complementary capabilities and one task-to-tool policy consumed by both Codex routing and the context-router MCP.
change.scope: Template code-intelligence configuration, bootstrap, validation, documentation, and tests.

options.summary: Swap CodeGraphContext for one new MCP entry and retain the current universal grep scripts and ad hoc bootstrap.

evidence.summary: A replacement MCP can be added without removing current commands.
The candidate tools process source locally.
Pinned packages can be checked without granting network access at runtime.
The existing MCP merge contract remains intact.
Existing bootstrap checks can verify command presence.
A bounded MCP entry change is revertible.

product_outcome.basis: One real graph is better than the dead package reference, but tool selection remains opaque.

business_outcome.basis: No measured downstream delivery effect yet.

correctness.basis: Parser-backed graph queries should outperform basename grep for supported structures.

maintainability.basis: The ad hoc bootstrap and duplicated detection logic remain.
maintainability.baseline: Tool behavior is distributed across bootstrap code and MCP JSON.
maintainability.result: The same distribution remains after a one-entry repair.

reliability.basis: The dead package call is removed, but health coverage remains partial.

transition_cost.basis: This is the smallest implementation change.

reversibility.basis: The change is a bounded configuration replacement.
reversibility.baseline: The current MCP configuration can be restored from the tracked repository state.
reversibility.result: The repaired MCP configuration can be restored through the same repository rollback.

total_cost.basis: Every future tool update still requires coordinated edits in multiple bootstrap and documentation surfaces.

options.summary: Replace the unshipped catalog and routing internals directly while preserving setup, bootstrap, MCP merge, and downstream ownership contracts.

evidence.summary: The existing context router and Engram remain available while the new graph path is introduced.
Selected default tools are local-first and do not require source upload.
The catalog pins versions and records licenses; install remains explicit and auditable.
Existing project-owned MCP entries are preserved and activation is additive during the staged transition.
Schema, plan, health, and benchmark fixtures can be deterministic template gates.
The catalog and generated entries are bounded tracked files; old scripts remain during canary rollout.

product_outcome.basis: Users gain one visible install/activation/health contract instead of hidden ad hoc behavior.

business_outcome.basis: Fewer exploratory reads should reduce agent latency and cost if the canary benchmark passes.

correctness.basis: Parser and LSP-backed tools replace language-blind grep for structural questions.

maintainability.basis: One catalog owns versions, licenses, roles, activation, install, and health metadata.
maintainability.baseline: Definitions are spread across .mcp.json, bootstrap code, docs, and optional shell checks.
maintainability.result: One machine-readable catalog becomes the decision owner and generated surfaces consume it.

reliability.basis: Pinned versions and per-tool health checks fail closed before activation.

performance.basis: Stack-aware activation is promising, but promotion requires a comparable local benchmark.

security.basis: License and source metadata become validated; remote-code latest installers are excluded from the default path.

transition_cost.basis: The catalog, validator, cross-platform adapter, tests, and canary measurement require more initial work.

reversibility.basis: Staged activation preserves the old path until explicit absence checks pass.
reversibility.baseline: The current bootstrap mixes detection, installation, configuration, and optional services in one script.
reversibility.result: The staged catalog can be disabled as one bounded layer while the existing bootstrap remains available during canary rollout.

total_cost.basis: Initial verification is larger, but future version and activation changes have one owner.

cleanup.removal_condition: Remove CodeGraphContext detection and demote grep graph scripts only after representative Windows and Linux canaries pass correctness and context-efficiency gates.
cleanup.absence_check: Search tracked template files and generated downstream fixtures for active codegraphcontext configuration and undocumented graph-script claims.

recommendation.reason: The catalog fixes the ownership failure, supports heterogeneous stacks, and makes token savings a measured promotion gate instead of marketing copy.
recommendation.rejected_alternative: A one-entry repair leaves the dead architecture around the new tool and cannot explain or verify why every downstream project receives the same dependencies.

envelope.outcome: Deliver the requested current ten-tool code-intelligence arsenal with stack-aware activation and verifiable efficiency.
envelope.scope: Template code-intelligence catalog, installer/checker, configuration, tests, documentation, and generated downstream contract.
envelope.risk_limit: No automatic activation of redundant MCP surfaces and no unreviewed non-commercial default dependency.
envelope.downtime_limit: Existing Engram and context-router workflows remain usable during transition.
envelope.cost_limit: No paid services or commercial licenses are introduced.
envelope.release_limit: No tag, push, release, or all-project rollout is included.
envelope.environment_limit: Implement and verify in the template plus temporary generated fixtures only; do not configure or index downstream projects.
envelope.rollback_requirement: Revert the bounded toolchain changes if schema, health, sync, or representative benchmark gates fail.
